chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ali ibn Ribat and Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who had children, and some of his children went missing, and he did not know where they were. The man died. What is done with the inheritance of the missing son from his father? He said: 'It is set aside (held in reserve) until he comes.' I said: 'Is Zakat due on his property?' He said: 'No, until he comes.' I said: 'When he comes, does he pay Zakat?' He said: 'No, until a full year passes while it is in his possession.' I said: 'If the man is lost and does not come?' He said: 'If the heirs of the man are numerous with his property, they divide it among themselves. If he comes, they return it to him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic inheritance rules for a missing person whose parent has died?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the fiqh of the *mafqud* (missing person), establishing that his reserved share is held in trust without immediate Zakat liability until his return or death is confirmed. It highlights the Shia principle of preserving the missing person's rights, ensuring that if he reappears, his share is returned provided a full lunar year (*hawl*) has passed since the inheritance came into his possession, balancing legal certainty with justice.
